title.narrative: EU Support to the fight against human trafficking and migrant smuggling in the Horn of Africa Region

description.narrative: In the region, along two main routes (the Central Mediterranean Route and the Eastern Corridor), nationals from countries such as Eritrea, Ethiopia, Somalia, Sudan, and South Sudan continue to migrate under vulnerable conditions, often embarking on perilous journeys. These routes are characterized by extreme weather conditions, legal and regulatory barriers, financial constraints, xenophobia, and limited access to protection services. Due to these challenges, migrants are frequently targeted by organised criminal networks and/or individuals offering false promises of safe and quick passage across international borders. However, migrants often find themselves trapped in situations of illegal detention for ransom, forced begging, and forced criminality.Although trafficking in human beings (THB) and smuggling of migrants (SoM) are distinct phenomena, together they constitute an illegal industry worth more than a multi-billion dollars. According to UNODC, human trafficking is one of the fastest-growing crimes, along with drugs and arms trafficking, and a highly profitable business, generating an estimated $150 billion in profits each year.[1]  The aim of this action is to improve the management of safe, orderly, and regular migration in the region and to support national authorities in addressing the smuggling of migrants (SoM) and trafficking in human beings (THB) within and from the Horn of Africa (HoA).The action is structured around two Specific Objectives (Outcomes):Strengthen the capacities of investigation actors, the judiciary, border and immigration authorities and improve access to protection services and sustainable solutions for Victims of Trafficking and vulnerable migrants through a rights-based approach, taking into account the gender specificity of the phenomenon and the particular vulnerability of women and children (BMM IV),¿Enhance the support to and continuation of regional/continental/international law enforcement cooperation in the fight against trafficking and smuggling networks whilst ensuring a smooth and balanced transition of the EU-funded Regional Operational Centre in support of the Khartoum Process (ROCK), currently based in Nairobi, to the AU continental Centre in Addis Ababa (ROCK III)
